sentiment.rationale: The document reports strong backward-looking results (adjusted EPS up 19% YoY, DTC operating income up 39% in Q4, Experiences record operating income) and raises forward guidance: management expects double-digit adjusted EPS growth in fiscal 2026, targets $7 billion in share repurchases (double the prior year), and increases the dividend by 50%. The guidance raise is organic, not attributed to one-time items or FX. However, the Q&A reveals a live carriage dispute with YouTube TV (a structural risk) and some lumpiness in content costs, which temper the score from a higher level. The overall tone is confident and forward-looking.

summary.revenue: Not disclosed (no specific revenue figure reported in the transcript).
summary.eps: Adjusted EPS for fiscal 2025 was up 19% from fiscal 2024. Over the past three fiscal years, a 19% compound annual growth rate in adjusted EPS.
summary.guidance: For fiscal 2026, expects to deliver double-digit adjusted EPS growth compared to the prior year. Targeting $7 billion in share repurchases in 2026 (double the $3.5 billion in fiscal 2025). Board declared a cash dividend of $1.50 per share, a 50% increase over the $1.00 paid in fiscal 2025.

Strong film slate for fiscal 2026 including Zootopia 2, Avatar: Fire and Ash, The Mandalorian and Grogu, Toy Story 5, live-action Moana, Avengers: Doomsday.
Experiences segment record operating income; two new cruise ships launching; expansion projects at all theme parks; new park in Abu Dhabi.
DTC streaming profitability improvement: Entertainment DTC operating income up 39% in Q4, full-year $1.3 billion (up $1.2 billion from prior year, $300 million ahead of original guidance).
AI deployment opportunities for personalization, user-generated content, and efficiency across the company.
